subject: ACME RAG eval — retriever & reranker next steps

Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME RAG eval — retriever & reranker next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet you and the ACME data team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from my side:

Recap:
- Goal: Improve retrieval grounding for product docs and reduce hallucinations in the support assistant.
- What we heard: short-form Q&A and multi-paragraph explainers are both common; latency target ~300ms p50 on the assistant.

Preliminary model recommendations (based on your sample):
- Retriever: hybrid approach (BM25 initial+dense embedding) with candidate pool ~200
- Embeddings: 1536-d dense embeddings (baseline using SBERT-style model)
- Generator: 13B instruction-tuned model for balance of cost/quality (we can test 7B and 70B variants)
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for top-10 re-ranking when precision matters; bi-encoder for high-throughput fallbacks

Attached: acme_rag_eval_results.csv (sample metrics), reranker_benchmark.pdf, prompt_set_v1.jsonl

Requests / next steps:
1) Can you share a redacted sample of 200-500 queries and a small S3 snapshot of product docs (or a link to the Drive folder)? This will let us run the full eval pipeline end-to-end.
2) We'll run: retrieval ablations (k candidates, chunk sizes), reranker comparisons (cross-encoder vs. bi-encoder), and prompt-set stability runs. Expect initial results in ~4 business days after we receive samples.
3) Quick 30-min sync next week to go over metrics and prioritization (I listed availability below).

Slack / contact: marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

—
Marissa Cole

1) Retriever settings: when you say candidate pool ~200, is that the number returned from BM25 before reranking or the final k you’d score? We typically see k=50 in production.
2) Grounding metrics: what exact metrics will you report so we can align on acceptance criteria?
3) Reranker latency trade-offs: can you share rough p95 latency estimates for cross-encoder vs. bi-encoder at our expected QPS (~20 qps)?

We can provide a redacted S3 snapshot and a 300-query sample. Happy to schedule the 30-min sync — Tue/Wed next week looks best for us.

Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval — retriever & reranker next steps

Great questions — answers below and a proposed plan.

1) Candidate pool vs. final k:
- "Candidate pool" = items returned by the initial retriever (BM25+dense hybrid). We recommend returning ~200 candidates from the retriever and then re-ranking the top 10 (k=10) with the cross-encoder when high precision is required. This gives a good tradeoff: recall upstream, precision downstream. If your production target is k=50, we can run that variant too — we'll include k=50 in the ablation matrix.

2) Grounding metrics (we'll publish these per prompt set):
- Precision@1 (is the top answer grounded in a retrieved doc?)
- Grounding rate (percentage of responses that cite a source with >=80% token overlap)
- Hallucination rate (manual label / automated heuristics)
- Utility score (human-rated relevance on 1-5)
- Latency (p50/p95 end-to-end and reranker-only)

Acceptance criteria (example): Precision@1 >= 85% and Hallucination rate <= 8% on the support prompt set. We can tailor thresholds to your product needs.

3) Reranker latency estimates (approx, based on our infra):
- Cross-encoder (re-rank top-10): p95 ~ 120–220ms additional, depending on model size and batch efficiency.
- Bi-encoder (dot-product re-scoring): p95 ~ 30–70ms, much lower but with lower re-rank quality on fine-grained grounding.

Plan & deliverables:
- Day 0 (receive samples): sanity-check and index
- Day 1–3: run ablations (k={50,200}, chunk_size={200,500}, overlap={20%}) and reranker comparisons
- Day 4: share detailed CSV and short slide deck with recommendations and preferred production profile (model + batching + caching suggestions)

Drive link to the eval notebook and scripts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-acme-rag-eval (shared).

Availability for 30-min: Tue 10–11am PT, Wed 2–4pm PT — let me know which works.

—
Marissa

Quick tech notes from our infra side that might help when you package the S3 snapshot:

- For embedding baselines we recommend 1536-d vectors saved as float32 parquet rows (schema + sample script attached in prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
- Chunking: 200–500 token chunk size with 20% overlap is our starting point. If docs are highly structured (tables/code), smaller chunks may help.
- Caching: we will enable prefix/KV caching for long-running sessions; if you have a traffic pattern with repeated queries, let us know — we can simulate and show cost benefits.
- Baseline scripts: we have an eval harness that runs retrieval->rerank->generation and outputs the CSV. I can push the exact scripts to the shared Drive folder after you confirm access.
